analysis.ambiguity1: The requirement "to order food on their phone while they are walking from class" is too vague regarding its platform target. It fails to specify whether the system must be delivered as a native mobile application (iOS/Android) or a mobile-responsive web application, affecting testing boundaries.
analysis.ambiguity2: The marketing requirement to "send push notifications to students at 11:30 AM" is ambiguous. It does not define how the system should handle OS-level user permission denials or how it manages delivery constraints if a student's device is completely offline in a basement classroom.
analysis.conflictSolution:
Conflict: The Chef needs the ability to mark items as "Sold Out" instantly to prevent invalid orders, but the IT Infrastructure Team warns that the basement Wi-Fi is terrible and the kitchen display system must operate offline for up to 10 minutes without crashing.

Resolution: Implement a local caching and queued synchronization layer on the Kitchen Display System (KDS). When the Chef marks an item as "Sold Out" during a network drop, the state is immediately applied to the local kitchen screen and queued. Once the Wi-Fi connection automatically re-establishes within the 10-minute threshold, the queued state updates sync to the cloud database, instantly updating the mobile application menu for students.
